items.en: make a song and dance about it
items.example: It's only a scratch, don't make a song and dance about it.
items.exampleTr: Sadece bir çizik, yaygara koparma.
items.simple: Make a lot of noise and fuss about something small.
dialogue: A: I told him I'd be ten minutes late.
B: And he had to make a song and dance about it?
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; 'make a fuss' un renkli hali.

items.tr: işi baştan kesmek, daha büyümeden önlemek
items.example: If the kids start arguing, nip it in the bud.
items.exampleTr: Çocuklar tartışmaya başlarsa daha büyümeden kes.
items.simple: Stop a problem when it is still very small, before it grows.
dialogue: A: Two people were late again this morning.
B: Let's nip it in the bud before it becomes a habit.
items.note: Kötü alışkanlık, dedikodu, sorun için.

items.example: Claiming that as a business lunch is sailing close to the wind.
items.exampleTr: Onu iş yemeği diye göstermek biraz sınırda gezinmek.
items.simple: Do something that is nearly not allowed, and you might get in trouble.
dialogue: A: I told my boss I was at the dentist, but I was at the football.
B: You like to sail close to the wind, don't you?
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; yasa, kural, ahlak sınırına yaklaşmak.

items.example: His plan to retire at forty is pie in the sky.
items.exampleTr: Kırkında emekli olma planı hayalden ibaret.
items.simple: A nice idea or plan that will almost surely never happen.
dialogue: A: The council says the new metro line will be ready next year.
B: That's pie in the sky.
items.note: Planı/vaadi küçümserken.

items.en: pull the rug out from under me
items.tr: ayağımın altındaki halıyı çekmek, beni yüzüstü bırakmak
items.example: They cancelled the funding and pulled the rug out from under me.
items.exampleTr: Finansmanı iptal edip ayağımın altındaki halıyı çektiler.
items.simple: Suddenly take away help someone was counting on.
dialogue: A: Why did you leave the band?
B: They decided to pull the rug out from under me a week before the tour.
items.note: 'me' kişiye göre değişir: 'pull the rug out from under them'.

items.example: Don't pass the buck, it was your idea.
items.exampleTr: Topu başkasına atma, senin fikrindi.
items.simple: Say a problem is someone else's job, so you don't have to deal with it.
dialogue: A: Who's going to tell the client?
B: Don't look at me. Typical, everyone wants to pass the buck.
items.note: ABD kökenli, her yerde yaygın; 'The buck stops here' = sorumluluk bende.

items.example: Put a sock in it, I'm trying to watch the film!
items.exampleTr: Kes sesini, filmi izlemeye çalışıyorum!
items.simple: A funny, rude way to tell someone to stop talking.
dialogue: A: And another thing about my boss...
B: Oh, put a sock in it, mate.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi, şakacı ama kaba; yakın arkadaş arasında.

items.example: I'm excited about this trip, so don't rain on my parade.
items.exampleTr: Bu gezi için heyecanlıyım, keyfimi kaçırma.
items.simple: Spoil someone's happy moment by saying something negative.
dialogue: A: You know it's going to rain all week in Rome?
B: Thanks for that. Way to rain on my parade.
items.note: 'my' kişiye göre değişir: 'rain on her parade'.

items.example: No wine for me, thanks. I'm on the wagon this month.
items.exampleTr: Bana şarap yok, sağ ol. Bu ay içkiyi bıraktım.
items.simple: Not drinking any alcohol for a while.
dialogue: A: Fancy a pint after work?
B: Can't, I'm on the wagon till Christmas.
items.note: 'fall off the wagon' = içkiye geri dönmek.

items.example: We can't just sweep it under the carpet and hope nobody notices.
items.exampleTr: Bunu halının altına süpürüp kimse fark etmesin diye umamayız.
items.simple: Hide a problem instead of dealing with it.
dialogue: A: Should we tell the client about the mistake?
B: Yes. We can't sweep it under the carpet.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'under the rug'.

items.example: He told a joke at the funeral. He really can't read the room.
items.exampleTr: Cenazede fıkra anlattı. Ortamı hiç okuyamıyor.
items.simple: Notice how people feel around you before you speak or act.
dialogue: A: Should I ask for a raise in today's meeting?
B: They just announced job cuts. Read the room!
items.note: Sosyal medyada da çok yaygın: 'Read the room, mate.'

items.example: Stop splitting hairs, it's basically the same thing.
items.exampleTr: Kılı kırk yarma, temelde aynı şey.
items.simple: Argue about tiny little differences that don't really matter.
dialogue: A: Technically it was five to nine, not nine.
B: Let's not split hairs.
items.note: Hafif sinirli: 'Now you're just splitting hairs.'

items.tr: iki ile ikiyi toplamak, durumu çakmak
items.example: I saw them leave together and put two and two together.
items.exampleTr: Birlikte çıktıklarını gördüm ve durumu çaktım.
items.simple: Use what you saw or heard to guess what's really going on.
dialogue: A: How did you know about the surprise?
B: Mum was hiding a cake. I just put two and two together.
items.note: Bazen 'put two and two together and make five' = yanlış sonuç çıkarmak.

items.example: Can we please not talk shop at dinner?
items.exampleTr: Yemekte lütfen iş konuşmasak?
items.simple: Talk about work when you're with colleagues outside work.
dialogue: A: So, about that budget meeting...
B: It's Friday night. Let's not talk shop.
items.note: Genelde şikâyet: 'No talking shop tonight!'

items.example: I haven't been ill all year, touch wood.
items.exampleTr: Bütün yıl hasta olmadım, nazar değmesin.
items.simple: Something people say so their good luck doesn't stop.
dialogue: A: How's the new car?
B: No problems so far, touch wood.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'knock on wood'. Söylerken tahtaya vurulur.

items.example: We had a fight years ago, but it's water under the bridge now.
items.exampleTr: Yıllar önce kavga ettik ama artık geçmişte kaldı.
items.simple: Something bad from the past that doesn't matter anymore.
dialogue: A: Sorry again about what I said at the wedding.
B: Forget it, it's water under the bridge.
items.note: Barışırken: 'Don't worry, it's water under the bridge.'

items.example: The trailer really whetted my appetite for the film.
items.exampleTr: Fragman filme olan merakımı iyice artırdı.
items.simple: Make you want more of something by giving you a little bit first.
dialogue: A: Did you like the first episode?
B: Yeah, it was enough to whet my appetite.
items.note: 'wet' değil 'whet' (bilemek). Mecazen ilgi uyandırmak.

items.example: The train was late again, but that's par for the course.
items.exampleTr: Tren yine gecikti ama bu olağan bir şey.
items.simple: Something bad that happens so often you expect it.
dialogue: A: The printer's jammed again.
B: That's par for the course in this office.
items.note: Golften gelir; genelde bıkkın bir kabulleniş.

items.example: The new boss has ruffled a few feathers already.
items.exampleTr: Yeni patron şimdiden birilerini rahatsız etti.
items.simple: Upset some people by changing things or saying what you think.
dialogue: A: I'm going to tell them their plan won't work.
B: Fair enough, but you might ruffle a few feathers.
items.note: Genelde değişim getiren kişi için, çok olumsuz değil.

items.example: Nobody asked you to stick your oar in.
items.exampleTr: Kimse senden burnunu sokmanı istemedi.
items.simple: Give your opinion when no one asked for it.
dialogue: A: I was only trying to help with their argument.
B: Well, you shouldn't stick your oar in.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi, gayriresmî, sitemli.

items.tr: kendi ayağına sıkmak, kendi kuyunu kazmak
items.example: If you skip the interview, you'll shoot yourself in the foot.
items.exampleTr: Mülakata gitmezsen kendi ayağına sıkarsın.
items.simple: Do something silly that ends up hurting you.
dialogue: A: I'm thinking of telling my boss what I really think of him.
B: Don't shoot yourself in the foot.
items.note: Zamir kişiye göre: 'He really shot himself in the foot.'

items.en: pull the wool over my eyes
items.example: Don't try to pull the wool over my eyes, I know you were out.
items.exampleTr: Gözümü boyamaya çalışma, dışarıda olduğunu biliyorum.
items.simple: Trick someone so they don't see what is really happening.
dialogue: A: I was studying all night, honest!
B: You can't pull the wool over my eyes.
items.note: 'my' kişiye göre değişir: 'pull the wool over their eyes'.

items.example: After three failed attempts, I threw in the towel.
items.exampleTr: Üç başarısız denemeden sonra pes ettim.
items.simple: Stop trying because you think you can't win.
dialogue: A: Are you still learning the guitar?
B: No, I decided to throw in the towel.
items.note: Boks'tan; Türkçedeki 'havlu atmak' ile birebir.

items.example: It took me a while, but then the penny dropped.
items.exampleTr: Biraz zaman aldı ama sonra jeton düştü.
items.simple: You finally understand something after not getting it for a while.
dialogue: A: When did you realise it was a surprise party?
B: When I saw the balloons, the penny dropped.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; Türkçedeki 'jeton düştü' ile aynı.

items.en: throw a spanner in the works
items.example: The rain threw a spanner in the works for our barbecue.
items.exampleTr: Yağmur mangal planımıza çomak soktu.
items.simple: Something that suddenly stops a plan from working.
dialogue: A: The venue just cancelled our booking.
B: Well, that's going to throw a spanner in the works.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'throw a wrench in the works'.

items.example: I really put my foot in it when I asked when the baby was due.
items.exampleTr: Bebeğin ne zaman doğacağını sorunca fena çam devirdim.
items.simple: Say something by mistake that upsets or embarrasses someone.
dialogue: A: Why is Jen so upset with you?
B: I put my foot in it about her haircut.
items.note: 'my' kişiye göre değişir: 'He put his foot in it.'
